answer.rationale: Finance requires an 18% cost cut and the incumbent has refused to renegotiate (renders 'negotiate_terms' infeasible per memory_c4 precedent; no margin to recover). Renewing the incumbent cannot meet the mandate. Adding a second source (memory_c3) spreads risk but does not achieve the mandated unit-cost reduction on its own — it adds complexity and cost without solving the price problem. Deferring (memory_c5) is inappropriate: the contract does not auto-renew, leaving a 14-day cliff, and the line is running at 94% of committed volume with no buffer — any service gap risks the production schedule. Switching primary to the low-cost vendor is the only action that achieves the 18% cut (they alone meet the mandate per memory_c2, where their invoicing stayed accurate and onboarding was quick last cycle). I want memory_c2 verified to confirm pricing/invoicing reliability of the low-cost vendor, and memory_c4 to confirm whether any residual leverage remains with the incumbent (likely minimal given their stated refusal). The line-at-94%-no-buffer context means a staggered or dual-track transition is warranted: sign with the low-cost vendor as primary now to lock the mandate-compliant price, but stage the volume ramp so the incumbent can absorb residual volume through month-to-month terms if needed (per memory_c5 precedent for non-critical continuity). This minimizes TCO without elevating delivery risk.
